verdicts.flaw_description: Two of the four cases have the outcome measured before the drip line was installed: the maize block was 'fitted 3 August' but the yield gain is recorded 'by 18 June', and the barley block was 'fitted 2 May' but measured 'by 17 March'. The other two cases (8 December to 23 February, 7 September to 22 November) run forward by about 2.5 months, so half the evidence is a gain that predates the intervention.

A named alternative cause both changed and reached the units: 'Pollen and airborne irritants in each group's district fell by half from the previous quarter, and every group lived and slept in unfiltered district air.' A halving of the exposure that triggers attacks, reaching every patient, fully accounts for 4-7 fewer attacks without the inhaler doing anything.

Two of the four classes have the score measured before the program began: Ashcombe 'started the program 6 December' but scored higher 'by 11 September', and Halloway 'started the program 20 June' but scored higher 'by 24 April'. The other two (8 January to 12 March, 6 July to 21 August) run forward about two months, so the reversed pair cannot be measuring an effect of the program.

The defect rate is computed on a narrower population than the claim: 'Rates cover the boards that reached the grading stage, and about a tenth of each run's boards were scrapped before grading.' Removing 10 percent of boards from the denominator before defects are counted can produce the 4-7 percent drop by itself. (The loosened optical threshold is a red herring, since 'every run here was graded at electrical test'.)
